title: Prachinburi Herbal Trip: Abhaibhubejhr, Cafes & Farms 2 Days | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A relaxed 2-day Prachinburi itinerary for herb and cafe lovers in Thailand: the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building, day spa, herbal coffee, and fruit-farm souvenir runs, with real spots and rough prices.
keywords: Prachinburi travel, Abhaibhubejhr, Prachinburi cafes, Prachinburi herbs, Prachinburi souvenirs
intro: Prachinburi is the kind of town that slows your heart rate, especially if you plan it as an herb-focused trip. Start at the yellow Baroque-style Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building, follow it with herbal coffee at the day spa, then stroll the fruit farms and grab something local to take home. This is an unhurried 2-day, 1-night plan that we've paced to match how this town actually moves.

blocks.html: A lot of people drive past Prachinburi on the way to Khao Yai without stopping, even though the town itself has good things tucked away quietly. The main draw is Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital, which has worked on Thai herbs and traditional Thai medicine for a long time. There's a museum inside an old building, a shop selling herbal products, and a day spa with a cafe built in. So this plan leans into the town's slow pace: walk unhurried, drink coffee, and pick up souvenirs you won't find anywhere else.

This herb-and-cafe plan suits anyone who wants an easygoing trip with no trekking or climbing. It's about a 2-hour drive from Bangkok to Prachinburi town, and it works for families bringing older relatives, couples, or even a solo trip. The best part is that everything sits within a short radius, so you're not driving long distances all day.

items: Duration — 2 days, 1 night is just right, not rushed enough to tire you out
Getting around — driving yourself is easiest, since some spots are scattered outside the town center
Budget — mid-range; food, coffee, and souvenirs are cheap, and town hotels start from high hundreds to low thousands of THB
Best time — November to February, when it's cool and comfortable for walking the farms without the heat

blocks.title: Check the days before you go
blocks.html: Abhaibhubejhr Day Spa is open Wednesday to Sunday, 9:00 AM–8:00 PM, closed Monday and Tuesday. If this is the anchor of your trip, avoid the start of the week. The museum in the old building keeps its own days off too, so a quick call ahead is the safest bet.

items.label: Day trips from Prachinburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.html: Day one covers the heart of the trip. Start at the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building in the morning before the sun gets harsh, then ease over to the cafe and day spa through late morning into the afternoon.

items.activity: Arrive at the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building inside Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital on Prachin Anuson Road
items.note: A yellow Baroque-style building over a century old, built in 1909, now a Thai traditional medicine museum. Free entry, and it photographs beautifully in the morning.

items.activity: Walk through the museum — old Thai herbal-medicine texts and traditional medical instruments
items.note: Takes a little over an hour. It's cool and comfortable inside, good for a slow walk while reading the signs as you go.

items.activity: Break for lunch at the Abhaibhubejhr Day Spa restaurant, focused on herbal dishes
items.note: It's in the green building on your left from the hospital entrance gate. Dishes run roughly 80–180 THB each.

items.activity: Follow up with fresh coffee at the cafe in front of the day spa, and try the herb-infused drinks
items.note: Coffee and drinks are about 50–90 THB. You can sit, catch the breeze, and take your time.

items.activity: Shop the Abhaibhubejhr herbal products — inhalers, balms, soaps, creams
items.note: These are easy souvenirs to grab. Prices start from tens to low hundreds of THB, so you can buy several to give away.

items.activity: Try booking an herbal or foot massage at the day spa if you have time left
items.note: Call to reserve a slot first, since evenings get busy. Service closes at 8:00 PM.

items.activity: Check into your hotel in town and rest
items.note: Hotels in town are easy to get to and make finding dinner simple.

blocks.title: About the spa
blocks.html: If you're set on a massage at the day spa, don't show up as a walk-in on a Saturday or Sunday — the queue is long. Call to book a day ahead to get the time you want. If you just want coffee and shopping, you can walk right in, no reservation needed.

Day two is an easy one. Head a little outside the town center to a field-view cafe, stop by a fruit market for fresh souvenirs, then head back. Wrap up before late afternoon so the drive home is relaxed.

items.activity: Have boat noodles for breakfast in town — Prachinburi is known for them
items.note: Popular spots like Kuaytiao Ruea Nai Tin or Mesa Sing run about 15–20 THB a bowl, so ordering several is easy on the wallet.

items.activity: Sit at a field-view cafe outside town and shoot the mountain views
items.note: Places like Myrrh Cafe have mountain views, or So Jaeng Slow Bar for coffee people. Drinks run about 60–120 THB.

items.activity: Stop by Nong Cha-om fruit market and buy seasonal fruit as souvenirs
items.note: In durian and mangosteen season, prices beat Bangkok — fresh from local orchards, with a little room to haggle.

items.activity: Lunch near the market or at a local roadside spot
items.note: Made-to-order Thai food or home-style places, roughly 60–120 THB per person.

items.activity: Finish with local crafts — woven palm-leaf bags or bamboo furniture
items.note: Prachinburi goods that are hard to find elsewhere. There are small, easy-to-carry pieces too.
The drive back to Bangkok is about 2 hours, getting you in just before evening.

blocks.text: Town cafes to add if you have extra time

blocks.html: Beyond the day spa cafe, Prachinburi town has several newer coffee shops that have been around a while and actually draw a crowd. If your trip can stretch another half day, fit a few more in.

items.name: 41 Cafetel
items.blurb: A central-town cafe with a relaxed fit-out and easy access, good for working or a break mid-walk

items.name: Myrrh Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe with wide mountain views, worth driving out to for photos and a morning sit in the breeze

items.name: So Jaeng Slow Bar
items.blurb: A slow-bar spot focused on drip coffee, good for anyone who likes sipping quietly

items: Abhaibhubejhr herbal products — inhalers, balms, soaps, creams; the town's standout souvenir, bought at the day spa shop
Seasonal fruit — durian and mangosteen from Nong Cha-om fruit market, fresh from local orchards
Woven palm-leaf bags — OTOP craft from village groups, handmade and lightweight
Prachantakham bamboo furniture — a local specialty, with both large pieces and small home decor items

blocks.title: Buy herbal products smartly
blocks.html: Buying Abhaibhubejhr products from the shop inside the hospital gets you the real thing at the straight price. Grab a small inhaler-and-balm set to give away — they're cheap and genuinely useful for everyone who receives one.

faq.q: Is the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building free to visit?
faq.a: The Thai traditional medicine museum inside the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building is open to visit free of charge. It's a yellow Baroque-style building over a century old, inside Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital on Prachin Anuson Road. Check the opening days ahead, since it has days off.

faq.q: Which days are the Abhaibhubejhr cafe and day spa open?
faq.a: Abhaibhubejhr Day Spa, which has a cafe, an herbal restaurant, and massage services, is open Wednesday to Sunday, 9:00 AM–8:00 PM, closed Monday and Tuesday. If you're planning a massage, call to reserve a slot first.

faq.q: How many days do you need for an herbal trip to Prachinburi?
faq.a: Two days and one night is just right. Day one covers the Abhaibhubejhr building, museum, cafe, and herbal souvenirs; day two is fruit farms, field cafes, and local souvenirs. If you only have one day, you can stick to the Abhaibhubejhr area alone.

faq.q: What Prachinburi souvenirs are worth buying?
faq.a: The standout souvenir is Abhaibhubejhr herbal products like inhalers, balms, soaps, and creams. After that come seasonal fruit from Nong Cha-om market, woven palm-leaf bags, and bamboo furniture from Prachantakham district.

faq.q: How long does it take to drive from Bangkok to Prachinburi?
faq.a: It's about a 2-hour drive from Bangkok to Prachinburi town, roughly 130 kilometers. The route is straightforward, and driving yourself is the most flexible, since the sights are spread across and beyond the town center.
